title: Entomophagy Among Mexican University Students: Dietary Perceptions and Analysis of the Acceptability of Consuming Insects (ACI)
content:
Entomophagy has been proposed as a sustainable food alternative due to the nutritional value of insects and their low environmental impact. However, its acceptance remains limited among various sectors of the population and has been insufficiently studied among university students. The aim of this study was to analyse the Acceptability of Consuming Insects (ACI) and food-related perceptions among university students in Mex-ico. An observational, analytical, cross-sectional study was conducted using a structured questionnaire based on previously validated scales designed to assess perceptions toward entomophagy. The instrument was validated using Cronbach’s alpha and McDonald’s omega coefficients. ACI was assessed using a six-point Likert scale, and associations were analyzed through chi-square tests and multivariate analyses (PCA and PERMANOVA).
The results showed that students recognized the nutritional and environmental benefits of insect consumption; however, barriers such as disgust, food neophobia and the visual appearance of insects were also identified. Two consumer profiles were distinguished: an innovative-rational profile and a traditional-neophobic profile. These findings indicate that perceptions of insect-based foods are influenced more by psychosocial factors than by demographic characteristics.
